defect.summary: THE ORDER WRITER ADMITS WHAT LEG B REFUSES (S199): mica-bridge's resolveOrderCitations admits a paper written at or before the chain's latest order, while leg B (gate4-sunset/index.ts, scope gate4Scope; papers counted in (prevOrderSeq, orderSeq)) counts each paper for one order, by sequenceNumber, across every declared invocation class and every subject the profile declares. A second order citing earlier papers is accepted by the writer and alarms at leg B. The writer cannot bind itself to the reader's rule without the reader exporting it: a bridge-side copy of the order rule is the second definition the cold refuter warned against.
defect.ground: Draft ARC_MICA-TICKET_S199-S206_DRAFT_v4_20261018.md (S199 v4: base a0d3017 / c9e3a9a, cond. 1 names gate4CountsAsOrder, the Rule prose = the cond.-2 alternative, audit 2026-10-18 13:23Z; this door-shaped machine ticket per audit 2026-10-18 14:22Z (1), the bridge half's opens, conditions and heads staying in the v4 markdown as the acceptance text); V1 cold refuter's S199 MAJOR 'P is the reader's own whole-chain predecessor'; signature pack ARC_MICA-PACK_Signature-Packs_20261017.md §6; dispatch CC3 (audit board 2026-10-17 19:22Z: 'S199 and S206 built as drafts (bridge halves on c9e3a9a; S199's machine half through the door)'). MECHANISM: one private gate4Orders(records, config) is the reader's order list (the declared warrantForm.invocation classes, whole chain); gate4OrderBound(records, config) exports the sequenceNumber of its last member or null, and THROWS on a profile gate4ProfileFault refuses (never null, which a writer would read as 'admit'); gate4Scope takes its orderSeq from gate4OrderBound and its order/predecessor from gate4Orders; leg B's invocations are gate4Orders. GATE4_ORDER_BOUND_RULE = "G4_ORDER_BOUND_V1" names the rule for the writer's booked refusal. No reading changes: every verdict on every gate4-sunset input is the reader's own (S199-1 compares the export against the printed orderSeq on every input the suite hands the reader).

arbiter.word: Granted by the audit under Frank's standing delegation, 2026-10-18, on the register item S199 and the rulings of 2026-10-18 06:56Z (3) and 13:23Z (§C): the machine exports its own order test and order bound (gate4CountsAsOrder, gate4OrderBound) so that the bridge's order writer refuses what leg B would refuse — a paper at or before the chain's latest order — and admits what leg B admits; no reading moves (every pre-existing gate4-sunset arm unchanged). Conditions of this signature: cond. 2 of the pair = the alternative — only an order whose own invocation class is declared is bounded, an undeclared subject's order books nothing and is not refused for another subject's P; the bridge half (s199-c2-bridge-on-c9e3a9a, 60be2c7 + the comment-only witness-fence fix) relays as a pair after this machine half, which lands first; S199's two dynamic specifiers in gate4-sunset.test.ts are rewritten as top-level import types in the signed tree (closure ruling 2026-10-18 15:4xZ (4)(ii)), so no closure entry is needed for S199; the ceiling stands as cond. 3 says — leg B reads form, never truth. expiresAt is the audit's fill and part of this signature.

conditions: 0. PAIRED WITH THE BRIDGE DRAFT (citadel branch s199-c2-bridge-on-c9e3a9a off c9e3a9a, the S199 commits): the bridge imports gate4OrderBound and gate4CountsAsOrder from the installed machine, so the bridge half cannot compile or start against a machine without these exports. RELAY ORDER: this machine relay FIRST, then the bridge. A bridge laid first refuses at ExecStart (loud), never silently.

1. gate4OrderBound(records, config) is the sequenceNumber of the latest record gate4Scope counts as an order, or null; gate4Scope calls it (one definition). gate4CountsAsOrder(entry, config) is the reader's per-record order test, the one gate4Orders filters by; it throws where the bound throws (cond. 2 alternative, audit 2026-10-18 06:56Z: the writer bounds only an order whose own class is declared). Arms: S199-1 (equal to the reader's printed orderSeq on every input the gate4-sunset suite gives the reader; a profile the gate blinds on makes the export throw and leg B CANNOT_ASSESS); S199-2 (two subjects' declared order classes: the other subject's later order is the bound, both orders); S199-3 (an undeclared class is not an order); S199-4 (a second declared invocation class counts; null with no order; throws on an absent or colliding profile); S199-5 (at bytes: gate4Scope reads gate4OrderBound and gate4Orders; the invocation filter is written once). S199-6 (gate4CountsAsOrder agrees with gate4Orders on every record of every reader input; the same eventType from an undeclared moduleId is no order; a second declared class is; throws on an absent or colliding profile; at bytes, both read gate4OrderTest). Mutants killed, transpile-only: a second, subject-filtered copy; the bound taken from the FIRST order; the bound returned null on a faulted profile; gate4Scope computing its own orderSeq by a subject-filtered rule. gate4CountsAsOrder: false on a faulted profile; matching on eventType alone; always true.
2. NO READING MOVES: every pre-existing gate4-sunset arm passes unchanged (55 at a0d3017; 61 with the six S199 arms).

3. WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX: the ceiling is the reader's, unchanged. Leg B reads FORM, never truth; a paper after the bound is a fresh paper, not a true one. The bound is only as good as the chain's sequence order (the reader's own trusted-order ceiling line). Under the served profile (to-wire-options builds ONE invocation class, the declared gate4 subject's ENDING_ORDERED) another subject's order is not an order to this reader and does not move the bound; the whole-chain rule bites only for classes the profile declares. The writer bounds only an order whose own class is declared: an undeclared subject's order is neither bounded nor refused (refusing it by another subject's bound is the ASK_ANSWERED shape).
